correlates.name: Rib fractures with pulmonary contusion
correlates.presentation: A 47-year-old driver hit the steering wheel in a high-speed crash. He has sharp left chest wall pain on every breath, bruising and point tenderness over the left 5th-8th ribs, and coughs a little blood. RR 26, HR 112, BP 118/76, SpO2 90%.
correlates.workup: Film: gaps in the cortex of four adjacent left ribs where they no longer line up, without callus; directly beneath them a patchy white airspace opacity that does not respect lobar borders.
correlates.management: More than 3 acute rib breaks generally means admission for observation rather than discharge.

correlates.name: Hiatal hernia
correlates.presentation: A 74-year-old woman with fullness after meals has a routine chest film before cataract surgery that shows a round gas-containing structure projecting over the heart. Afebrile, no cough or sputum, WBC 7,200/mm3, lungs clear on exam.
correlates.workup: Frontal film: inside the round structure over the heart, gas sits above a straight horizontal fluid level with debris; the lateral film places it behind the heart, continuous with the upper abdomen; lungs clear.

correlates.name: Pneumoperitoneum
correlates.presentation: A 62-year-old man had sudden severe upper abdominal pain 6 hours ago that has spread across the whole abdomen. He lies still; the abdomen is rigid with rebound tenderness and absent bowel sounds. T 38.1 C, HR 118, BP 102/64.
correlates.workup: Upright chest film: a thin curved crescent of gas beneath the right hemidiaphragm, separating it from the top of the liver; on the lateral view the gas sits anteriorly under the diaphragm.
